summary: The read-gate eval (scripts/eval-read-gate.ts, `npm run eval:read-gate`) has a runnable harness and committed per-case tables: with the gate on, mean cost per run on a 49 KB file was $0.077 vs $0.124 (-38%) on Sonnet and $0.171 vs $0.243 (-30%) on Opus, and -1% and 0% on a 19 KB file, where an earlier version of the gate had cost Opus 20% more. The work-view SQLite benchmark (scripts/benchmark-work-view.ts) has its synthetic-fixture and approximately 3 GB real-database latencies summarized in docs/development/viewer-sync-recovery.md; the real database is not in the repository, raw reports from both benchmarks go to a gitignored reports/ directory, and the read-gate eval needs paid model calls. The Smart Explore comparison (17.8x fewer tokens for discovery, 19.4x for targeted reads) is a written A/B report with no script in the repository, and the README and CHANGELOG figures (~10x, 90%, 200x) are stated without data.
result_focus_note: manual classification of published_results: outcome = does the tool do its job; engineering = speed of the software itself
